frontal_lobe.name: Frontal Lobe
frontal_lobe.description: The front part of each cerebral hemisphere. It handles planning, decision-making, personality and voluntary movement. The gyri shown here are the superior and middle frontal gyri, the precentral gyrus and the orbital gyri.
facts: The precentral gyrus is the primary motor cortex, which controls voluntary movement.
The prefrontal cortex, at the very front, is involved in planning and self-control.
In most people, Broca's area in the left frontal lobe helps produce speech.
Separated from the parietal lobe by the central sulcus.

parietal_lobe.name: Parietal Lobe
parietal_lobe.description: The upper middle part of each hemisphere. It processes touch, temperature and pain and helps with spatial awareness. Shown here: the postcentral, supramarginal and angular gyri.
facts: The postcentral gyrus is the primary somatosensory cortex, which receives touch signals from the body.
Helps judge where the body and objects are in space.
The angular gyrus is involved in reading and understanding language.

temporal_lobe.name: Temporal Lobe
temporal_lobe.description: The lower side part of each hemisphere, near the ears. It processes hearing, language and memory. Shown here: the superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri and the fusiform gyrus.
facts: The primary auditory cortex, which processes sound, is in the superior temporal gyrus.
In most people, Wernicke's area in the left temporal lobe helps understand language.
The fusiform gyrus is involved in recognising faces.

occipital_lobe.name: Occipital Lobe
occipital_lobe.description: The back part of each hemisphere. It is the brain's main centre for vision.
facts: Contains the primary visual cortex.
The left occipital lobe processes what we see on the right side, and the other way round.
Damage here can cause loss of part of the visual field.

insula.name: Insula
insula.description: A region of cortex folded deep inside the lateral sulcus, hidden under the frontal, parietal and temporal lobes.
facts: Involved in sensing the body's internal state, such as heartbeat and hunger.
Plays a role in taste and in emotions such as disgust.
Turn on X-ray to see it beneath the outer lobes.

limbic_system.name: Limbic System
limbic_system.description: A group of structures involved in memory and emotion. Shown here: the cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, hippocampus, amygdala and fornix.
facts: The hippocampus is essential for forming new memories.
The amygdala helps process emotions, especially fear.
The fornix is a bundle of nerve fibres that carries signals out of the hippocampus.
The hippocampus is named after the Greek word for seahorse because of its shape.

corpus_callosum.name: Corpus Callosum
corpus_callosum.description: A thick band of nerve fibres that connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
facts: It is the largest bundle of white matter in the brain.
Contains about 200 million nerve fibres.
Lets the two hemispheres share information.

thalamus.name: Thalamus
thalamus.description: A pair of egg-shaped structures deep in the brain that relay sensory and motor signals to the cortex.
facts: Almost all sensory information except smell passes through the thalamus on its way to the cortex.
Also plays a role in sleep, alertness and consciousness.
There is one thalamus in each hemisphere.

basal_ganglia.name: Basal Ganglia
basal_ganglia.description: Groups of nerve cells deep in the brain that help control movement and habits. Shown here: the caudate nucleus and putamen.
facts: Help start wanted movements and stop unwanted ones.
Parkinson's disease affects the circuits of the basal ganglia.
The caudate nucleus and putamen together form the striatum.

hypothalamus.name: Hypothalamus
hypothalamus.description: A small region below the thalamus that controls body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep, and links the nervous system to the hormone system.
facts: Controls the pituitary gland.
Acts like the body's thermostat.
Is about the size of an almond.

pituitary_gland.name: Pituitary Gland
pituitary_gland.description: A pea-sized gland below the hypothalamus that releases hormones controlling growth, metabolism and other glands.
facts: Often called the master gland because it controls several other hormone glands.
Sits in a hollow of the sphenoid bone called the sella turcica.
Releases growth hormone among many others.

optic_chiasm.name: Optic Chiasm
optic_chiasm.description: The X-shaped place where the optic nerves from the two eyes meet and partly cross.
facts: Fibres from the inner half of each retina cross to the other side here.
Lies just in front of the pituitary gland.

brainstem.name: Brainstem
brainstem.description: The stalk connecting the brain to the spinal cord, made of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata. It controls automatic functions such as breathing and heart rate.
facts: The medulla oblongata helps control breathing, heart rate and blood pressure.
The pons relays signals between the cerebrum and the cerebellum.
Most cranial nerves come out of the brainstem.

cerebellum.name: Cerebellum
cerebellum.description: The 'little brain' at the back, below the cerebrum. It coordinates movement, balance and posture.
facts: Contains more than half of the brain's neurons, though it is only about 10% of its volume.
Helps make movements smooth and accurate.
Involved in learning motor skills such as riding a bike.
